Short answer: In modern unified-memory GPUs, bandwidth-bound decoding latency is governed by how well the attention kernel can keep the memory subsystem saturated without stalling on L1/L2 cache misses, shared-memory reuse, or DRAM latency. Hybrid linear attention reduces the working set and improves spatial locality, while full attention is more sensitive to DRAM bandwidth and capacity. LPDDR5X (or HBM2e/5 on high-end GPUs) sets the ultimate ceiling; L1/L2 and shared memory are the levers that determine how close you get to that ceiling.

Notes:
- “Lock-free style” here means:

  - No Python-level locks; concurrency is simulated via threads.
